name: v0.0.1 - Begin Match
body:
> [!IMPORTANT]
> **This is the first public preview, and it will be buggy.** Read the known issues below and the [full release notes](https://github.com/Jstar269/nakagawa-recomp/blob/v0.0.1/docs/RELEASE_NOTES_v0.0.1.md) before you start, and please tell us what breaks.

Nakagawa Recomp turns the program code of a PSP game you own into a native Windows program. It translates the game's MIPS code to C ahead of time, links it with a native runtime, and runs it through SDL3 and Vulkan. Your games, saves and fonts stay on your PC.

## Highlights

- **Hot Shots Tennis is playable.** Hot Shots Tennis (UCUS98701) runs at its native 30 frames per second in menus and in matches on the reference PC (Ryzen 9 5900X, RTX 3080).
- **Bring your own disc, as it is.** Add an `.iso` made from a UMD you own, or the `EBOOT.PBP` of a PSN release of a UMD game, which the player turns back into its disc image. The player decrypts the game's encrypted program files on your PC, the way PPSSPP does. PSP system software (firmware) is never decrypted.
- **Works offline.** The ZIP carries every build tool **BUILD PACKAGE** needs (Python, the MSYS2 compiler, GNU Make, SDL3), checked against a pinned manifest. Nothing is downloaded.
- **A real launcher.** Library cards with each disc's own icon, a four-stage build you can watch and cancel, saved settings, controller setup with live input, keyboard rebinding, and a performance overlay on `F3`.
- **Pause anywhere.** `Esc`, `F1` or the controller's Guide button freezes the game, its sound and its clock. The pause has no menu yet.
- **Your PSP's own fonts.** Copy the font files from your own PSP ([how](https://github.com/Jstar269/nakagawa-recomp/blob/v0.0.1/docs/SETUP.md#copying-the-fonts-from-your-psp)) and import them in **Settings > PSP FONTS**; games then draw their text with them. All 18 system fonts import. They are optional.
- **Honest failures.** When a game needs something that isn't supported yet, the player stops and names what is missing instead of faking it.

## Get started

1. Download `nakagawa-recomp-0.0.1-windows-x64.zip` below and check it (next section).
2. Extract it and run `bin\nakagawa_player.exe`.
3. Drag in your game's `.iso`, click **BUILD PACKAGE**, then **Play**.

New to Nakagawa? [Can I play it?](https://github.com/Jstar269/nakagawa-recomp/blob/v0.0.1/README.md#can-i-play-it) explains what you need and what to expect.

**You need:** Windows 11 x64, a Vulkan-capable GPU, 8 GB RAM (16 GB recommended), 5 GB of free disk space, and your own copy of the game as an uncompressed `.iso` (or a PSN release's `EBOOT.PBP`). Nothing from Sony is included: no games, game data, firmware or fonts.

## Check your download

v0.0.1 isn't code-signed, so Windows SmartScreen may warn the first time you run it. Please don't turn SmartScreen off; check the download instead.

1. In the folder you downloaded to, this must print the same value as `nakagawa-recomp-0.0.1-windows-x64.zip.sha256`:

   ```powershell
   (Get-FileHash .\nakagawa-recomp-0.0.1-windows-x64.zip -Algorithm SHA256).Hash.ToLower()
   ```

2. After extracting, in the extracted folder, this proves the player was built by this repository's release workflow from commit `d1c7d80dfeaae4d6b94254b8c3158c2d319b8f9d`, the commit this release is tagged at (SLSA Build Level 2). It needs the [GitHub CLI](https://cli.github.com/), signed in once with `gh auth login`:

   ```powershell
   gh attestation verify .\bin\nakagawa_player.exe --repo Jstar269/nakagawa-recomp `
     --signer-workflow Jstar269/nakagawa-recomp/.github/workflows/provenance-attestation.yml `
     --source-ref refs/heads/main --source-digest d1c7d80dfeaae4d6b94254b8c3158c2d319b8f9d
   ```

`SHA256SUMS.txt` in the ZIP lists every file's SHA-256. If a check fails, don't run the file; report it.

**If Windows Security blocks the player.** Some PCs have the Microsoft Defender rule "Block executable files from running unless they meet a prevalence, age, or trusted list criteria" turned on. It is an attack surface reduction rule, off by default on home PCs, and some security tools turn it on. That rule blocks `nakagawa_player.exe`, because it is new, and every game package the player builds, because each one is built on your PC. Explorer then says Windows "cannot access the specified device, path, or file", and **Windows Security > Virus & threat protection > Protection history** shows "Risky action blocked". Whoever manages that rule can exclude the folder you extracted Nakagawa to and `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Nakagawa\data\packages` from it ([Microsoft's guide](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-endpoint/troubleshoot-asr)). Check the download as above first, and please don't turn Defender or SmartScreen off.

## Known issues

- **Few other games work yet.** Hot Shots Tennis is the one game rated Playable. Other games range from gameplay to a black screen (see the table below). A game that draws no new frame for 30 seconds gets an offer to keep waiting or stop; a game stuck on a black screen does not, so use **STOP GAME** in the player ([#308](https://github.com/Jstar269/nakagawa-recomp/issues/308)).
- **Sound:** a few late sound wakes remain, mostly while loading ([#1296](https://github.com/Jstar269/nakagawa-recomp/issues/1296)), and some ATRAC3 sound effects fail to decode ([#1096](https://github.com/Jstar269/nakagawa-recomp/issues/1096)).
- **Movies.** Some movies, Hot Shots Tennis's included, show a black screen, play slowly and their sound cuts in and out. The game itself plays normally ([#1049](https://github.com/Jstar269/nakagawa-recomp/issues/1049), [#279](https://github.com/Jstar269/nakagawa-recomp/issues/279)).
- **Only PSN releases of UMD games** convert. PSP minis, games tied to the PSP that bought them, PSOne Classics and PGD-protected game data aren't supported yet.
- **No networking** or ad hoc play.
- **Windows only** for playing; Linux is for development for now ([#306](https://github.com/Jstar269/nakagawa-recomp/issues/306)).

The full list of known issues is in the [release notes](https://github.com/Jstar269/nakagawa-recomp/blob/v0.0.1/docs/RELEASE_NOTES_v0.0.1.md#known-issues).

## Games tried for this release

On the maintainer's own copies, with the release build: add the game, **BUILD PACKAGE** offline with the bundled tools, then about seven minutes of play. How far a game gets on your PC may differ. None of these runs crashed or logged an error.

| Game | How far it got | What you see |
|---|---|---|
| Hot Shots Tennis | Menus and matches | **Playable**, at its native 30 frames per second |
| PAC-MAN Championship Edition | Gameplay | Plays timed games through to results and awards, at 60 frames per second |
| Gravity Crash Portable | Gameplay | Plays its training level, at its native 30 frames per second |
| STREET FIGHTER ALPHA3 MAX | Title and attract-mode fight demo | Shows its normal first-start save notice, then runs very slowly with garbled intro graphics |
| Half-Minute Hero | Title, menus, name entry, story intro | Waits at the first chapter card |
| Mega Man Maverick Hunter X | First screen | Stays on its first screen |
| LocoRoco | Language select | Black screen after the language select |
| FINAL FANTASY III | Loading icon | Black screen after the loading icon |
| Super Stardust Portable | Nothing shown | Black screen |
| PATAPON | Nothing shown | Black screen; after 30 seconds the player offers to stop it |
| Hot Shots Golf: Open Tee 2 | Builds, stops at launch | A message names the call that isn't supported yet |
| Wipeout Pure | Doesn't build | **BUILD PACKAGE** stops: one of its modules is in a format not supported yet |
| Dragon Ball Z: Tenkaichi Tag Team | Refused when added | The copy tried was a modified dump, which the player refuses; a clean dump hasn't been tried |

On a black screen or a stuck first screen, use **STOP GAME** in the player.

Tell us how far other games get in [Compatibility reports](https://github.com/Jstar269/nakagawa-recomp/discussions/categories/compatibility-reports).

## Downloads

| File | Size | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| `nakagawa-recomp-0.0.1-windows-x64.zip` | 285 MB (951 MB, 10,639 files extracted) | The player, its public source and the bundled build tools |
| `nakagawa-recomp-0.0.1-windows-x64.zip.sha256` | | The ZIP's SHA-256 |
| `nakagawa-recomp-0.0.1-prerequisite-sources.zip` and its `.sha256` | 525 MB | The source of every bundled build tool; you don't need it to play |

## Report a problem

Use the [Smoke Test Report](https://github.com/Jstar269/nakagawa-recomp/issues/new?template=smoke_test_report.yml) form for bugs, post how far a game gets in [Compatibility reports](https://github.com/Jstar269/nakagawa-recomp/discussions/categories/compatibility-reports), and ask questions in [Help](https://github.com/Jstar269/nakagawa-recomp/discussions/categories/help). **Copy details** on an error card puts a short report on your clipboard. Read logs before attaching them: they should contain no disc images, game files or personal paths.

## Thanks

To [@gufernandess](https://github.com/gufernandess), [@Apurvbkt](https://github.com/Apurvbkt) and [@Nitjsefnie](https://github.com/Nitjsefnie) for their contributions to this release.
